actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 396 - 0 (Roll no. 251). (text: CR H4654)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 396 - 0 (Roll no. 251). (text: CR H4654)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4671)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8823.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4654-4656)
Mr. Walberg moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees using workers' compensation medical benefits, employing agencies, and medical providers convicted of fraud.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Labor may suspend payments to a provider of services, appliances, or supplies... if the provider has been convicted of fraud

dimensions.assessment: Allows the complete suspension of payments to specific medical providers convicted of fraud within federal or state healthcare and workers' comp programs.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Labor may suspend payments to a provider of services, appliances, or supplies... if the provider has been convicted of fraud

dimensions.assessment: May result in savings or reduced fraudulent payouts under the federal workers' compensation program, though exact fiscal amounts are not stated.
Amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act to add explicit suspension authority and requires the Secretary of Labor to issue regulations.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall promulgate regulations to carry out this subsection.

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory authority for the Department of Labor to apply to payments made 180 days after enactment and onward.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to payments made to a provider... on or after the date that is 180 days

missing_information: Estimated monetary savings from suspending fraudulent provider payments
Specific criteria the Secretary will use in promulgated regulations
importance_detail.rationale: This bill permits the Department of Labor to suspend federal workers' compensation payments to medical providers who have been convicted of fraud relating to federal or state health care programs. It strengthens administrative enforcement tools against convicted providers.
